chunks: 981 - Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from him that he said:

Nuh عليه السلام used to say when he entered the morning and evening: “O Allah, I make You witness that whatever blessing and well-being in religion or worldly life has come to me in the morning and evening is from You alone, having no partner. To You belongs all praise, and to You belongs thanks for it upon me until You are pleased, and after pleasure.”

He would say it ten times when morning came and ten times when evening came, and because of that he was called a grateful servant. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to say after salat al-fajr (prayer):

“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and sorrow, incapacity and laziness, stinginess and cowardice, the burden of debt and the dominance of men, the ruin of the unmarried, heedlessness, humiliation, hardness, poverty, and destitution. And I seek refuge in You from a soul that is not satisfied, a heart that does not humble itself, an eye that does not shed tears, a supplication that is not heard, and a salat (prayer) that does not benefit. And I seek refuge in You from a woman who makes me old before the time of my old age, and I seek refuge in You from a child who becomes increase against me, and I seek refuge in You from wealth that becomes a punishment against me, and I seek refuge in You from a deceitful companion who, if he sees a good deed, buries it, and if he sees an evil deed, spreads it. O Allah, do not place for a wicked person over me any hand or favor.”

key_terms.الشُّكْرُ: gratitude and thankful acknowledgment to Allah
key_terms.نِعْمَةٍ: blessing bestowed by Allah in religion or worldly life

ai.seo_question: What supplications are recommended for the morning and evening in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches morning and evening supplications centered on gratitude to Allah and seeking refuge from spiritual, emotional, social, and worldly harms. It links constant thankfulness with the وصف of being a grateful servant and preserves a supplication of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم after salat al-fajr (prayer).
